---
title: ENCODE
description: The ENCODE portal's experiment and file inventory as resource tables, files referenced by URI, never copied.
---

The [ENCODE portal](https://www.encodeproject.org) catalogs experiments and
the files they produced. The release lands both inventories from the portal's
`report.tsv` with an explicit field list, released, archived and revoked alike,
and derives `resource.encode__experiment` and `resource.encode__file`: assay,
biosample, target, lab, and per file the format, assembly, size, checksum and
`href` or S3 URI. The first use is making BEDbase's ENCODE accessions
resolvable. The portal publishes no release number, so the version is the
retrieval date and raw holds the latest crawl only.

## Licence and citation

ENCODE's [data use policy](https://www.encodeproject.org/help/citing-encode/):
"External data users may freely download, analyze and publish results based on
any ENCODE data without restrictions". Citation of the ENCODE Consortium and
the producing lab is requested.

## Join keys

- `resource_id` is spelled `encode:ENCSR…` / `encode:ENCFF…`, exactly as BEDbase writes its targets, so the two join with `=`.
- `resource.resource_relationship` carries file → dataset, and experiment → biosample term and target gene; biosample terms join `ontology.term`, target genes join `annotation.ncbi__gene`.
- `taxon_id` comes from the biosample organism.

## Good to know

- The columns are a declared subset of each object's properties, landed whole in rows but not in fields; adding a field is a re-land.
- Cells are unquoted upstream and lists are comma-joined, so a list whose values contain commas cannot be split back.
- Annotation, Reference and Series datasets share the `ENCSR` space with experiments but are not landed, so a file's `dataset` resolves in `resource.encode__experiment` only when `dataset_type` is `experiments`.
